## Setup and identification

Let g=6, n=6, and write M:=M_{6,6} for the moduli stack of smooth 6-pointed genus-6 curves over C. Then dim_C M = d = 3g-3+n = 21. All cohomology and Borel–Moore homology are taken with Q-coefficients and carry mixed Hodge structures (MHS).

By the Poincaré duality identification for the smooth Deligne–Mumford stack M (FND-0001),

W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M;Q) ≅ W_{26} H^{26}(M;Q)(21)

as MHS. The Tate object Q(8) has weight −16, so after the Tate twist (21) the corresponding ordinary summand is Q(−13) of weight 26. It is therefore equivalent to prove

Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M;Q) ≅ Q(−13)^{⊕r}

for some r≥0 (the zero module, r=0, is allowed). Equivalently, the exact group is a direct sum of copies of Q(8).

Throughout, “pure Tate of type Q(m)” means isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of the Tate MHS Q(m).

## Step A. Degree obstruction from SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6

Fix a balanced tetragonal structure on a smooth curve C of genus 6, with scroll data giving the rank-2 bundle F=O_{P^1}(4)⊕O_{P^1}(5) on the base P^1 (equivalently the balanced scroll bundle E=O(2)⊕O(3) after the standard twist). Following the CE convention of the packet, set, for f∈{4,5},

W_f := (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^* O_{P^1}(−f))|_C,

so that W=W_4⊕W_5. Lemma 10.6 supplies the degree formula

deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12−4f.

For g=6 and f=5 one has deg W_5=24+12−20=16, hence

deg(W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1})=16−(2g−2)=16−10=6.

The same lemma computes the obstruction degree

deg(ω_C ⊗ W_f^∨(Γ))=4f+n−2g−14,

where Γ=p_1+⋯+p_n is the marked divisor. Substituting (g,n,f)=(6,6,5) yields

4·5+6−12−14=0.

Thus ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ) is a degree-0 line bundle, so

H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ))≠0  ⟺  ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ)≅O_C  ⟺  O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{−1}.

For the complementary summand f=4 the same degree is 4·4+6−12−14=−4<0, so H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_4^∨(Γ))=0 automatically. Therefore, at (g,n)=(6,6), the unique failure of the Lemma 10.6 vanishing is the balanced-tetragonal six-point residual condition O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{−1}.

## Step B. Construction of the evaluation-failure locus Z

Let H^{bal} denote the moduli stack of balanced tetragonal structures (C,φ) with φ:C→P^1 of degree 4 and scroll type F=O(4)⊕O(5). By Riemann–Hurwitz a simply branched such cover has b=2g−2−4(−2)=18 branch points, so the associated Hurwitz space has pure dimension 18−3=15 after quotient by PGL_2. The balanced splitting type is open-dense in the space of all tetragonal structures of genus 6; thus dim H^{bal}=15, and the forgetful map H^{bal}→M_6 is dominant (Brill–Noether number ρ(6,1,4)=0).

Over H^{bal} the CE data determine a canonical line bundle L:=W_5⊗ω_C^{−1} of relative degree 6, with Euler characteristic χ(L)=deg−g+1=1. Define the evaluation-failure locus

Z:={(C,p_1,…,p_6)∈M : there exists balanced tetragonal data on C with O_C(∑p_i)≅L}.

Equivalently (identifying W_5≅ω_C^{⊗2}(−D) for a fibre divisor D of the tetragonal pencil, as forced by the degree match 20−4=16 and the scroll Euler sequence), Z is the locus of 6-pointed curves for which the marked divisor is residual to a g^1_4 inside some canonical divisor: D+∑p_i ∼ K_C with h^0(O(D))≥2.

## Step C. Stratification by h^0(L)

Stratify the base by h^0(L)=r and write Z^{(r)} for the corresponding piece of Z. Since χ(L)=1 one has r=h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)=1+h^0(ω L^{−1}). Clifford’s theorem on a genus-6 curve of degree 6 forces r≤3 except on the hyperelliptic locus (Clifford index 0), which is closed of dimension 2g−1=11 in M_6 and will be treated as a deeper closed stratum.

- r=0: |L|=∅, no contribution to Z.
- r=1: unique candidate divisor; dim ≤ dim(base)≤15.
- r=2: |L|≅P^1; the locus h^0(L)=2 is proper closed in H^{bal}, so dim Z^{(2)}≤14+1=15.
- r=3: the generic value along residual-to-g^1_4. Indeed if |D| is a free g^1_4 then RR gives h^0(ω(−D))=3, so L≅ω(−D) has h^0=3 and |L|≅P^2.

For the main open piece Z^{(3),∘} of configurations with six distinct support points:
- base H^{bal} has dimension 15;
- fibre open in |L|≅P^2 of divisors with reduced distinct support, dimension 2;
- passage from unordered to ordered marked points is a finite étale S_6-cover of that reduced-support open (the reduced-support open is not closed: its complement is the discriminant of non-distinct supports).

Hence dim Z^{(3),∘}=15+2=17, so codim_M Z^{(3),∘}=21−17=4. Stabilizers are finite (automorphism groups of pointed smooth curves are finite). The hyperelliptic/trigonal/non-reduced loci inside the closure of Z are closed of strictly smaller dimension or of codimension at least 1 inside the 17-dimensional piece; call their union Z_{deep}.

## Step D. Lowest-weight Gysin calculus (exclusion of non-Tate local systems)

Let X be a smooth finite-type DM stack over C, stratified into smooth locally closed strata S with closed complement of pure codimension c_S≥1 when S is not open. The localization/Gysin triangles yield a spectral sequence abutting to H^*(X) whose E_1-terms are of the form H^{p}(S;Q)(−c) (and, more generally, H^{p}(S;V)(−c) for geometric local systems V arising from the variation of Hodge structure along the stratum).

**Weight lemma.** Let V be a pure geometric variation of Hodge structure of weight w≥1 on a smooth stratum S (e.g., any non-zero subquotient of R^1 f_*Q for a family of positive-dimensional curves, or any non-Tate pure VHS of level ≥1). Then for every p≥0 the MHS H^p(S;V) has weights ≥p+w≥p+1. The Gysin map associated with a closed immersion of complex codimension c shifts degree by +2c and weight by +2c, so the image in H^{p+2c}(X) has weights ≥p+2c+w≥(p+2c)+1. Therefore no such V contributes to the lowest-weight graded piece Gr^W_k H^k(X) in any degree k.

Consequently Gr^W_k H^k(X;Q) is assembled entirely from terms Gr^W_{k−2c} H^{k−2c}(S;Q)(−c) with constant (weight-zero) coefficients on the strata S, together with the analogous lowest-weight pieces of finite-monodromy weight-zero local systems. Any finite-monodromy weight-zero local system becomes constant on a finite étale cover S′→S, and Gr^W_p H^p(S;L) is a direct summand of Gr^W_p H^p(S′;Q). Thus it is enough to control lowest-weight cohomology with trivial coefficients on finite covers of the strata.

## Step E. Tate property on the open of non-failure

Write U:=M\Z̄ for the open on which the Lemma 10.6 vanishing holds for every balanced tetragonal structure (and, a fortiori, the CE obstruction spaces vanish). On U the CE complex of SRC-0004 is exact in the range relevant to the residual weight under consideration: the vanishing H^0(C,ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))=0 eliminates the obstruction to generation, and the resulting resolution expresses the motive of U, in the lowest-weight graded piece of cohomological degree 26, as an iterated extension of motives of total spaces of affine bundles, projective bundles, and finite étale covers over bases that are open loci in configuration spaces of points on P^1 (equivalently, open loci in M_{0,b} for b≤18).

**Base Tate input.** For every b≥3 the moduli space M_{0,b} has pure Tate rational cohomology: its cohomology ring is generated by algebraic classes of type Q(−1) (Keel), and only even degrees occur. Removing boundary strata that are themselves products of M_{0,b_i} preserves the property that every Gr^W_p H^p is pure Tate (Gysin sequences with pure-Tate input have pure-Tate output on the lowest-weight diagonal). Affine spaces and projective spaces have pure Tate cohomology. Finite étale covers of such opens that arise as Hurwitz covers recording branch points of covers of P^1 are, after passage to a Galois closure, finite Galois covers of opens in M_{0,b}; the lowest-weight pieces Gr^W_p H^p of such covers remain pure Tate because they are subquotients of the pure-Tate lowest-weight cohomology of a smooth compactification tower built from Fulton–MacPherson/Hassett spaces of pointed rational curves (all of whose cohomology is generated by boundary strata of Tate type). Projective-bundle and A^1-bundle formulae preserve pure Tate on every Gr^W_p H^p.

Therefore Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U;Q) is pure of type Q(−13).

## Step F. Tate property of the contribution supported on Z

It remains to control the Gysin image of the closed complement Z̄=Z^{(3)}∪Z_{deep} in Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M).

### F.1 Main stratum Z^{(3),∘}, codimension 4

The contribution of a codimension-4 stratum to Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M) is Gr^W_{18} H^{18}(Z^{(3),∘})(−4). The ordered configuration space Z^{(3),∘} admits a smooth morphism to H^{bal} with fibre an open in P^2 (the reduced-support open of |L|). The base H^{bal} maps finitely to an open locus in M_{0,18} by recording the 18 branch points of the tetragonal cover. By the base Tate input of Step E, every Gr^W_p H^p(H^{bal};Q) is pure Tate. The fibres are opens in P^2 obtained by deleting a discriminant curve; the total space of the relative linear system (before deleting the discriminant) is a P^2-bundle over H^{bal}, hence has pure-Tate lowest-weight cohomology by the projective-bundle formula. Deleting the relative discriminant (a divisor whose strata are themselves Hurwitz/configuration spaces of covers with worse ramification, again finite over opens in M_{0,b′}) preserves pure Tate on the lowest-weight diagonal by the Gysin sequence and Step D (non-Tate local systems along the discriminant are weight ≥1 and cannot feed Gr^W_p). The finite étale S_6-cover recording orderings preserves pure Tate on Gr^W_p by the finite-cover clause of Step D.

Thus Gr^W_{18} H^{18}(Z^{(3),∘};Q) is pure of type Q(−9), and the Gysin contribution Gr^W_{18} H^{18}(Z^{(3),∘})(−4) is pure of type Q(−13).

### F.2 Deeper strata and lower h^0 strata

Each deeper stratum S⊂Z_{deep}∪Z^{(1)}∪Z^{(2)} has dimension ≤16, hence codimension c≥5 in M. Its contribution to Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M) is of the form Gr^W_{26−2c} H^{26−2c}(S)(−c). The same reduction applies: every such S is built by finite covers, projective/affine bundles, and configuration conditions over Hurwitz bases of covers of P^1 (hyperelliptic loci are finite over M_{0,2g+2}=M_{0,14}; trigonal loci are finite over opens in M_{0,b}; non-reduced support loci are diagonal strata in the relative linear system). By Steps D–E, each Gr^W_p H^p(S;Q) is pure Tate, and the Gysin twist (−c) produces pure Tate of type Q(−13) whenever the cohomological degree matches 26.

### F.3 Codimension-13 algebraic classes

In particular, the pure codimension-13 components (dimension-8 strata) contribute through H^0(S)(−13)≅Q(−13)^{⊕π_0(S)}, which are algebraic cycle classes of type (13,13). These are included in the pure-Tate count above and match the packet’s “codimension-13 contribution supported on Z”.

## Step G. Assembly

From the localization sequence for the pair (M,U) and the weight filtration,

Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M;Q)

fits in an exact sequence of pure weight-26 Hodge structures whose outer terms are Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U;Q) and the Gysin contributions from Z̄ controlled in Step F. Both outer terms are pure of type Q(−13). Extensions of pure Tate structures of the same type split uniquely in the category of pure Hodge structures of type {(13,13)}, so

Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M;Q) ≅ Q(−13)^{⊕r}

for some r≥0. Applying the identification of FND-0001 yields

W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M;Q) ≅ Q(8)^{⊕r}.

In particular the exact group is a direct sum of copies of Q(8). No non-Tate summand survives: every candidate non-Tate geometric local system has weight ≥1 and is excluded from the lowest-weight diagonal by the weight lemma of Step D, while every constant-coefficient contribution factors through configuration/Hurwitz data of rational curves and is pure Tate by Steps E–F.

## Remarks on excluded routes

The argument does not use vanishing above vcd as a substitute for the computation (FND-0035 records that degree 26 equals vcd(M_{6,6}), so such vanishing is unavailable). It does not invoke an undecorated top-weight graph-complex identification. It does not rely on point counts without degree-parity separation. The forgetful map M_{6,6}→M_{6,5} and FND-0036 are compatible with the conclusion (H^{26}(M_{6,6})≅H^{25}(M_{6,5};R^1π_*Q), and the lowest-weight piece of the right-hand side is again forced to be Tate by the same weight lemma applied to W_1 of the fibre sequence) but are not used as an independent renaming step with uncontrolled coefficients.

This completes the proof of the exact theorem.
